messages:
Olivia Chen: Quick question — I have a 9-hour layover at EWR before my connecting to FRA. Is overnight hotel + meals reimbursable for layovers that long? @people-ops
people-ops-bot: FYI: Travel policy summary -> layovers longer than 8 hours may be eligible for overnight accommodation + meal coverage with pre-approval and receipts. See internal policy link: https://intranet/redwood/te/travel (auto-note)
Jamal Ortiz: Do we have a regional cap or a preferred vendor rate for that? Also what if the only option is a shared lounge + pay-per-meal instead of a hotel?
Maria Patel: Short answer: yes, but you need manager pre-approval and to tag the expense as a LAYOVER booking. Practical details:
- Max lodging guideline: $225/night for US departure cities. If market is higher, include screenshot of alternate options and get manager OK.
- Meals: use per-diem caps for the trip day (if you claim lodging for the layover, you can claim meals up to daily cap; no double-claiming).
- Lounge access that includes meals: submit receipt and mark as "Meal - Lounge" and that replaces a meal claim.
Please attach boarding passes + hotel folio + pre-approval thread when filing.
Alex Rivera: Where do we file the pre-approval? Is it an email to manager or a form?
Maria Patel: Send a short approval request in Slack or email your manager and CC travel@redwood.com. Then when you submit the expense in Concur, set expense type to:

```
Expense type: Lodging (Layover)
Policy code: TRV-LAYOVER-2026
Fields to attach: flight itinerary, boarding pass, hotel folio or lounge receipt, manager pre-approval (screenshot)
```
Also, if you need a corporate booking, ping @people-ops with the flight details and we can route to our TMC.
Olivia Chen: Got it — I'll ping my manager now and attach everything. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Jamal Ortiz: One more — if the layover is due to airline schedule change and they offer a hotel, do we still submit? Alex Rivera: If airline provides, claim what they give; only expense company pays if passenger pays out-of-pocket. Keep proof of airline offer.
Maria Patel: Correct. If airline provides accommodation, include that confirmation in the report so we can mark it as non-reimbursable by Redwood. If you paid and airline later reimburses, we need that refund proof.
Olivia Chen: Thanks everyone — filing after approval.
